image-to-text-converter.formula:
OCR pipeline (Tesseract 5):
1. Binarise: separate dark text pixels from the light background.
2. Segment: group pixels into text lines, then words, then characters.
3. Recognise: a trained neural network classifies each character shape.
4. Correct: a language dictionary fixes likely misreads.
Example: a 800 x 200 screenshot with the words HELLO WORLD ->
the engine segments 2 words, 10 letters, and returns "HELLO WORLD".

image-to-text-converter.workedExample:
Recognise the words HELLO WORLD from an 800 x 200 screenshot.
1. The engine binarises the image: dark letters on a light background.
2. Segmentation finds 2 text lines collapsed into 1 line, 2 words, 10 characters.
3. The neural network classifies each character: H-E-L-L-O (space) W-O-R-L-D.
4. The English dictionary confirms both words are valid.
5. Output: the plain text "HELLO WORLD", ready to copy or download as .txt.
Messy photos add errors at each step, which is why clean screenshots work best.
